content.text: {"what_it_is": {"claims": [{"text": "Survivable Airborne Operations Center (SAOC), program element 0604288F, is a U.S. Air Force development program funded in the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Air Force account.", "citation": {"fact_id": "59341ea3a81146ce"}}, {"text": "The SAOC, designated the E-4C, replaces the aging E-4B fleet, which faces capability gaps, diminishing manufacturing sources, rising maintenance costs, and parts obsolescence as it nears the end of its serviceable life.", "citation": {"fact_id": "5fb4968f51510b59"}}, {"text": "SAOC is intended to give the President, the Secretary of Defense, and the Joint Chiefs of Staff a worldwide, survivable, enduring node of the National Military Command System to ensure continuity of operations and continuity of government during a national emergency or after ground command-and-control centers are lost.", "citation": {"fact_id": "5fb4968f51510b59"}}, {"text": "The program fulfills the Air Force nuclear mission by providing Nuclear Command, Control and Communications (NC3) capabilities so the President can command and control U.S. military nuclear-weapons operations.", "citation": {"fact_id": "5fb4968f51510b59"}}, {"text": "The SAOC weapon system comprises a Commercial Derivative Aircraft (CDA), a mission system, and ground support systems.", "citation": {"fact_id": "6e467bb9a898b8f4"}}, {"text": "The aircraft is to be hardened against nuclear and electromagnetic effects and modified with aerial-refueling capability for sustained airborne operations, while the mission system integrates secure communications and planning on a modern IT infrastructure built on a Modular Open System Approach (MOSA).", "citation": {"fact_id": "6e467bb9a898b8f4"}}, {"text": "Ground systems for the program include aircrew trainers, mission-crew trainers, maintenance training devices, ground support equipment, and test and sustainment system-integration laboratories to enable operations, sustainment, and future modifications across the weapon system's lifecycle.", "citation": {"fact_id": "6e467bb9a898b8f4"}}]}, "why_it_matters": {"claims": [{"text": "The program's total funding grows from $1,617,187 thousand in FY2025 to $1,833,128 thousand (about $1.83 billion) requested for FY2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "37d3935deb9ca02d"}}, {"text": "That is a year-over-year increase of $215,941 thousand (roughly $216 million) from FY2025 to FY2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "b407bae4275e9f89"}}, {"text": "In FY2024 the program recorded actual spending of $717,641 thousand (about $718 million), so the FY2026 request is more than two-and-a-half times its FY2024 execution level.", "citation": {"fact_id": "59341ea3a81146ce"}}, {"text": "The FY2026 request is almost entirely discretionary: a discretionary request of $1,826,328 thousand (about $1.83 billion) makes up the bulk of the total.", "citation": {"fact_id": "dad3cd7e1a9bab7e"}}, {"text": "A small reconciliation (mandatory) request of $6,800 thousand (about $6.8 million) is added to the discretionary base to reach the $1,833,128 thousand FY2026 total.", "citation": {"fact_id": "a35fffbcde2a41e4"}}, {"text": "The money flows through a single named project, the Survivable Airborne Operations Center, funded at about $1,826.3 million in the FY2026 budget year.", "citation": {"fact_id": "ee398dbccb09b510"}}, {"text": "That same SAOC project line was funded at about $1,617.2 million in the current year (FY2025) and about $717.6 million in the prior year (FY2024), showing the program's rapid growth as development advances.", "citation": {"fact_id": "b25a684cfbff8132"}}]}, "players": {"claims": [{"text": "The program is run by the U.S. Air Force, with funding drawn from the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Air Force appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "d9d10855ed669668"}}, {"text": "The program's users are the President, the Secretary of Defense, and the Joint Chiefs of Staff, whom SAOC is designed to serve as a survivable airborne node of the National Military Command System.", "citation": {"fact_id": "5fb4968f51510b59"}}, {"text": "Program funding also supports program-office operations and management services, including Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs) and Advisory and Assistance Services (A&AS), alongside Interim Contractor Support during development.", "citation": {"fact_id": "5fb4968f51510b59"}}]}, "recent_developments": {"claims": []}}
